audience: Halo 4 owners who walk their dog daily
key_takeaways: Map lag creates anxiety even when the dog is safe
Participants judge GPS quality by how quickly the dot catches up after movement

evidence_quotes: I almost turned back because I thought she got out.
When the dot lags it makes me nervous.

pain_points: Map position noticeably behind actual location in open areas
current_workarounds: Visually scanning the park instead of trusting the map alone
jobs_to_be_done: Know my dog's location confidently during off-leash time
moments_that_matter: First few seconds after a sudden direction change

opportunities.opportunity: Surface GPS freshness indicator on map
opportunities.notes: Could reduce false-alarm anxiety when signal is stale

recommended_action: Prototype a 'last updated' or signal-strength cue on the live map and test with 5 more walkers.
open_questions: Does lag correlate with LTE vs Wi-Fi?
How often does lag occur vs user noticing it?
